document.control_rule: The DVWA user-manager policy page states admin-only access. Admin is the allowed control; fixture-documented non-admin is the candidate; anonymous is the expected-denied control. If both non-admin and anonymous receive the same protected object, classify broad exposure under this explicit policy rather than as a candidate-specific bypass. A denied candidate with matching admin and anonymous controls is a negative fit.

interpretation_rules.broad_exposure: admin resource visible and the same object is visible to both documented non-admin candidate and anonymous expected-denied control; policy breach, fit 3, outcome explicitly labeled broad_exposure
interpretation_rules.candidate_denied: admin allowed and both non-admin candidate and anonymous expected-denied control cannot see the resource; confirmed negative fit 1
interpretation_rules.candidate_specific: admin resource visible, documented non-admin candidate visible, anonymous control denied; fit 3

pilot_protocol.acceptance: A usable live scoring.v4 profile requires all nine scenarios, complete source/request counts, contemporaneous independent controls, frozen hash/timestamp, and validation before selector execution. This calibration alone cannot assert missing permission or session oracle proof.

controls.access_control: Use fixture-stated admin-only user manager, a fresh existing non-admin session, admin allowed control, non-admin denied/allowed response, and object/action identity. Avoid modification endpoints.
controls.brute_force: Compare rejected and accepted credential attempts with identity evidence and a fresh session distinct from the framework session. Marker-only remains partial.
controls.sqli: Compare candidate response against benign, negative, or complementary query on the same form and security level; inspect response evidence independent of method-agent verdict.

failure_inventory: A visible response may reflect input or an existing authorized login rather than proving exploitation.
An admin session cannot prove an Access Control violation; use the existing fixture-documented non-admin user.
A changing userId parameter may be ignored by the tested endpoint; require object-specific response change.
The DVWA brute-force form may report accepted credentials without creating a new identity-bound session.
High-security blind SQLi can add random delay to misses; require matched controls and repeated separation.
Known static payloads can fail despite a vulnerable fixture; preserve inconclusive results and do not infer infeasibility.
Network, login, security-level, or scope failures invalidate dependent comparisons.
A preliminary literature preference is not empirical proof of a method ordering in this fixture.
